quote: Newly minted quadriplegics are not as sad, six months later, as they expect to be, etc.
content: The finding is being remembered in the direction that helps. The classic study found that accident victims a year after their injury rated their happiness well below controls, and far below the lottery winners they were compared with; the surprise was that the gap was smaller than outsiders predicted, not that it closed (Brickman, Coates & Janoff-Bulman 1978). Later work with larger samples found that long-term disability produces a substantial and lasting drop in life satisfaction with only partial adaptation over years (Lucas 2007), and reviews of spinal-cord injury place subjective well-being persistently below population norms. "Quadriplegics deal, and so would you" is the affective-forecasting literature's point that people overestimate the durability of their reactions; it is not evidence that the feared thing turns out fine, and the essay's technique does not need that stronger claim to work.

quote: Be a true coward, and plan out your retreat in detail—visualize every step—preferably before you first come to the battlefield.
content: This is good advice and it is one of the few prescriptions in the sequence with independent support. Mentally contrasting a desired outcome with the obstacles to it, and planning the response to the obstacles, is the procedure that Oettingen's program found actually improves effort and outcomes, in contrast to positive fantasy alone (Kappes & Oettingen 2011); defensive pessimism, the strategy of imagining what could go wrong and preparing for it, outperforms forced optimism for the people who use it; and decatastrophizing, walking a feared scenario through to its manageable consequences, is a standard and effective element of cognitive therapy. The essay's mechanism, that a scenario one can imagine surviving becomes one whose probability one can assess, is the same mechanism those literatures describe. Where the annotations part company with the essay is only at its last sentence, which supposes that theists who visualized atheism would abandon theism; the visualization is good practice regardless of where it leads.
